subject.title: Feature request: Mid-stream message injection (soft steer)

question: Should OpenClaw scope this issue to a refreshed ordinary-message admission fix, or define a new true soft-steer lifecycle that can pause or abort active generation and resume with injected context?
rationale: Current main has partial boundary-steering fixes, but the requested behavior changes session-state ownership, delivery ordering, runtime interruption, and fallback semantics that code inspection cannot choose safely.

options.title: Refresh Admission Path
options.body: Refresh or replace https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/89238 so ordinary same-session messages reach active-run queue policy, while keeping broader pause/resume semantics tracked separately.

options.title: Define New Soft-Steer Mode
options.body: Specify a new queue/control mode with explicit abort, partial-output, context-resume, and backend-compatibility semantics before implementation.

options.title: Limit To Boundary Steering
options.body: Document current boundary steering plus `/queue interrupt` as the supported behavior and close broader pause/resume work only after a maintainer explicitly rejects it.

recommendation.title: Refresh Admission Path
recommendation.body: Refresh or replace https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/89238 so ordinary same-session messages reach active-run queue policy, while keeping broader pause/resume semantics tracked separately.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent has the strongest combined signal across current steering blame, protected branch history, and adjacent session-state lifecycle work.
